extracted.intended_audience: readers and writers of natural history / travelogues; naturalists and general educated readers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance embedded in a travel/natural-history chapter on how to observe, explain, and report animals, habitats, and local phenomena; aimed at producing thorough, evidence-based descriptive natural history.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not treat habits and instincts as fixed points
rubrics_metrics.description: It has generally been the custom of writers on Natural History to take the habits and instincts of animals as fixed points; this assumption is however an arbitrary one, and has the bad effect of stifling inquiry into the nature and causes of 'instincts and habits.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reject the arbitrary assumption that habits/instincts are unchangeable; avoid using them as final explanations. Instead, use them as phenomena to be investigated rather than as fixed axioms that halt further inquiry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain habits by reference to structure and environment
rubrics_metrics.description: I believe that a careful consideration of the structure of a species, and of the peculiar physical and organic conditions by which it is surrounded, or has been surrounded in past ages, will often... throw much light on the origin of its habits and instincts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When accounting for an animal's behaviour, connect morphological/anatomical features and present or historical environmental conditions to the habit; use comparative anatomy and ecological context as explanatory tools (illustrated here by the Maleo's foot structure explaining its nesting habits).

rubrics_metrics.name: Relate structure and habits through variation and natural selection
rubrics_metrics.description: These again, combined with changes in external conditions, react upon structure, and by means of 'variation' and 'natural selection', both are kept in harmony.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret correlations between form and behaviour in an evolutionary framework: consider how variation and selection, along with changing external conditions, could produce the observed harmony between structure and habit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report precise empirical measurements and quantitative data
rubrics_metrics.description: Good rice produces thirty-fold... the eggs... four to four and a half inches long by two and a quarter or two and a half wide. No less than 191 species have been discovered... the list of land birds, 144 in number...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support descriptive claims with exact measurements, counts, species totals, ranges and quantitative comparisons. Use such data to justify assertions about abundance, completeness of sampling, and the distinctiveness of regional faunas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use firsthand empirical observations and anecdotes for credibility
rubrics_metrics.description: At one of the smaller, marginal jets which I managed to approach, I held my hand to see if it was really as hot as it looked, when a little drop of mud that spurted on to my finger scalded like boiling water.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include direct, on-the-spot observations and short personal experiments or incidents to illustrate conditions and to lend authority and vividness to accounts; factual anecdote strengthens descriptive reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain behaviour by anatomical detail (use morphology as causal evidence)
rubrics_metrics.description: In the structure of the feet of this bird, we may detect a cause for its departing from the habits of its nearest allies... The toes are... strongly webbed at the base, forming a broad powerful foot, which... is well adapted to scratch away the loose sand...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When proposing why a species exhibits particular habits, point to specific anatomical features and explain mechanistically how those features enable or constrain the behaviour; use comparative examples with related taxa to support causal inferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be explicit about sampling effort and geographic/comparative context
rubrics_metrics.description: I myself assiduously collected birds in Celebes for nearly ten months... collections of birds had also been sent to Holland... yet all their researches combined have only added eight species...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State your fieldwork duration, sampling coverage, and reference comparisons to other collectors/regions to justify claims about species lists or completeness; situate local findings within broader geographic and historical collection efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use vivid sensory description to convey place and phenomena
rubrics_metrics.description: A picturesque path among plantations and ravines brought us to a beautiful circular basin... It was filled with clear water very near the boiling point, and emitted clouds of steam with a strong sulphureous odour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ concrete sensory details (visual, olfactory, tactile, temperature, motion) and precise spatial description to create vivid scenes and make natural phenomena comprehensible and memorable to readers.
